The Volt profiler couldn't write its output in the sandbox (EPERM), so I'll profile directly with Node's built-in `--cpu-prof`, writing only to `/tmp`.
`isPrime` is the hottest function in `scripts/slow.mjs`, using about 624 ms of self time, roughly 88% of the samples. Its caller `countPrimes` accounts for about 632 ms in total.

The naive trial-division loop runs up to `n` for every prime below 60,000, which is what makes it expensive. `dedupe` is a distant second at about 24 ms, because the 9,000-element `includes` scans are native and fast.

Volt's profiler (`ide profile cpu`) failed to write its output in this sandbox (EPERM), so I profiled with `node --cpu-prof` and wrote the profile to `/tmp/slow-prof`. No project files were changed.
